title: Plan AG: AI Resume Optimization
summary: Job analysis → quantified achievements → rewrite → layout → iterate on applications
scenario: For job seekers who need to quickly tailor a resume to a specific role — turning a generic resume into a high-match version.

steps.title: Job analysis
steps.detail: Paste the full job description and have the model extract hard requirements, nice-to-haves and implied skills, then flag which of your experiences map to them. Know what the hiring side wants before you write a word.
steps.tips: Ask for a 'JD keyword list + your matching points' output so the rewrite is targeted.

steps.title: Quantified achievements
steps.detail: Rewrite each experience as 'action verb + what you did + quantified result' and let the model add numeric framing. If you lack hard numbers, use ranges, frequency or time saved as proxies.
steps.tips: Every bullet needs at least one number — it's the single biggest filter for getting past screening.

steps.title: Rewrite
steps.detail: Reorder experiences by relevance to the role and weave JD keywords naturally into experience and skills sections. Fact-check every line — models will embellish.
steps.tips: Keep your real data and duties; let the AI handle expression, never fabrication.

steps.title: Layout
steps.detail: Use a single-column template with consistent fonts and spacing, kept to one page (junior) or two (senior). Run a keyword-density check and keep the layout ATS-parseable.
steps.tips: Avoid tables and graphic layouts — ATS parsing breaks; plain text structure is safest.

steps.title: Iterate on applications
steps.detail: Before each application, tweak keyword order and emphasis to the JD, then pass it through a grammar tool. Track responses and refine after a few rounds.
steps.tips: Two silent applications to the same role means swap the keyword set and retry — don't stick to one version.

pitfalls.title: Letting AI fabricate experience
pitfalls.detail: Models over-polish and even invent data; one deep interview question exposes it. Everything must be true and verifiable.

pitfalls.title: One resume for every job
pitfalls.detail: Match rate decides screening; tailor keywords per role.

pitfalls.title: Fancy layouts
pitfalls.detail: Trendy templates fail ATS and read as amateur; clean single-column wins.

pitfalls.title: Writing without testing
pitfalls.detail: Have the model role-play the interviewer and ask 5 questions, then prepare answers.
